messages:
emily.w: Heads-up — getting multiple restore failures for tenant-99 snapshots. Objects missing encryption metadata (no SSE header / no CMEK tag). Seen on backup objects uploaded between 00:10–00:40 UTC. https://console.storage/tenant-99/snap-2026-03-21.tar.gz
raj.patel: Which uploader job wrote those? any recent deploys?
marta: We did an IAM prune last night around 23:50. I warned about the uploader SA but thought perms were safe. Could be related.
emily.w: Logs show 403 on kms:Encrypt for the uploader service account during PutObject. Quick check command I ran: 
```
# aws example
aws s3api head-object --bucket redwood-backups --key tenant-99/snap-2026-03-21.tar.gz
# gsutil
gsutil stat gs://redwood-backups/tenant-99/snap-2026-03-21.tar.gz
```
opsbot: Alert INC-2026 created: backup-restore-failures-tenant-99 (severity: high)
raj.patel: I pulled audit logs with this filter: 
```
resource.type="gcs_bucket" AND protoPayload.methodName="storage.objects.insert" AND timestamp>="2026-03-21T00:00:00Z" AND timestamp<="2026-03-21T01:00:00Z"
```
I can see PutObject entries but they all have no encryption metadata attached. Also found KMS denies: 
```
protoPayload.status.code=7 AND protoPayload.authenticationInfo.principalEmail:"backup-uploader@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com"
```
emily.w: If objects were uploaded without SSE/CMEK, they're effectively unencrypted at rest (or using provider default). For S3 we could do an in-place copy and set SSE-KMS header, e.g.: 
```
aws s3 cp s3://redwood-backups/tenant-99/snap-2026-03-21.tar.gz s3://redwood-backups/tenant-99/snap-2026-03-21.tar.gz --metadata-directive REPLACE --sse aws:kms --sse-kms-key-id arn:aws:kms:...:key/abcd
```
But that still needs kms:Encrypt permission.
marta: Short-term mitigation: re-grant the uploader SA kms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter and storage.objectAdmin for the affected buckets, then re-run the upload job to recreate properly tagged objects. I'll prepare RBAC rollback.
oncall-sre: Oncall here — I'll apply a timeboxed grant (48h) and kick off replay for tenant-99. Please confirm the exact SA and resources.
emily.w: Service account is backup-uploader@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com. Buckets: redwood-backups (us-central1). Patch and then run the job: `k8s job backup-uploader --replay --tenant=tenant-99`
raj.patel: Noted an audit sink gap between 00:15–00:25 where Storage Object Create events are missing from our central logging (sink returned 500s). I'll open a telemetry ticket — could be related to ingestion throttling during the RBAC daemon rollout.
compliance-bot: Potential data exposure flagged: snapshot contains user CSV exports. Required: notify compliance within 1 hour and start content-scan.
marta: I'm opening a compliance ticket and looping in legal. Also adding a blocker to the RBAC cleanup PR to prevent automatic prune until we have a preflight that asserts KMS grants.
emily.w: Action items: (1) oncall-sre temporary grant + replay (2) raj to investigate audit sink gap and attach logs (3) marta to update RBAC PR and add preflight check (4) emily/raj/marta own postmortem + runbook.
oncall-sre: Grant applied, replay started, will update progress in INC-2026. If replay fails due to missing object re-encryption capability we will fallback to re-uploader instance that streams objects through a service with KMS perms.
raj.patel: Also recommend adding this pre-deploy check to CI: verify uploader SA has kms:Encrypt & storage.objects.create in the target project/bucket via an automated iam-sim test.
emily.w: Agreed — postmortem owners set: emily.w, raj.patel, marta. We should add a new checklist item to encryptops playbook: verify KMS grants + object metadata sample before any RBAC prune.
marta: filing SEC-2026 and will create a short blameless incident note with timeline. DMing legal now. :white_check_mark:
opsbot: Created ticket SEC-2026 and linked INC-2026.
emily.w: Thanks all — please escalate if anything new shows up.
